gaps.note: Not a known concept and not explained or linked on this page; the reader knows permutation matrices but not the partial variant or its at-most-one-1-per-row-and-column property.

gaps.term: shear realized by the network, gates commute with shear
gaps.quote: Gates commute with a common shear, so they run on sheared streams.
gaps.note: Asserted without citation or explanation; the page never says how the gates of the linear network act on a sheared array or why they commute with a shear.

gaps.quote: Each edge $e$ changes that shear by $G_e$, the difference of its end-vertex matrices
gaps.note: The page never says the network's vertices carry matrices, so the reader cannot tell what the end-vertex matrices or their difference are; the cited claim stands in for how the network realizes a shear.

gaps.quote: a field splits into $\beta$ pieces of width $u/\beta$
gaps.note: The page does not explain why the network's matrix size beta determines the number of pieces a field splits into.

gaps.quote: Each edge needs $\operatorname{rank}G_e$ of these interchanges
gaps.note: Cited, but the page does not say why the argument for the shear A (rank A interchanges) carries over to the edge matrix G_e on pieces of width u/beta.

gaps.term: one swap per one of Pi
gaps.quote: Each one is one swap, so the shear takes $\operatorname{rank}A$ interchanges.
gaps.note: The page never explains how a single 1 in the matrix Pi corresponds to one interchange of two fields.
The page does not justify this: it needs that invertible factors preserve rank and that a partial permutation matrix has rank equal to its number of ones; neither is stated.
The page does not say what the calls are (the same interchange procedure on width u/beta) or what a level is before using the word.
The page does not show that the R calls, each on volume V/W at width u/beta, cost lambda V phi(u/beta) in total; the recurrence is asserted from the level cost.
The condition R < beta W is never derived or justified on the page, yet the whole recurrence argument depends on it.
Width u/beta^l equals 1 only when u is an exact power of beta, which the page does not state; ell = log_beta u need not be an integer.
Asserted without argument: the reader is not shown why swapping single-bit fields costs constant time per stored bit.
The page asserts that the logarithm is O(u^tau) without justification; the reader is not told that a logarithm grows more slowly than any positive power.
